title: GPU-Direct Collective: Scalable Communication and Collective Operations on Modern GPUs
problem: Collective communication operations become bottlenecks in GPU clusters as they scale to thousands of GPUs, limiting application performance and efficiency.
motivation: Efficient collective communication is critical for HPC applications on GPU clusters. Poor scaling of communication limits overall system performance at scale.
method: The framework enables GPUs to send data directly to each other (called GPU-direct memory access) instead of routing through the CPU. It also offloads collective operations—coordinated tasks where all GPUs need to exchange or combine data—to specialized hardware, freeing the CPU to do other work. Together, these prevent communication from becoming a bottleneck, allowing the system to scale nearly linearly across thousands of GPUs.
key_novelty: Combining direct GPU-to-GPU communication with hardware offload enables efficient collective operations even when coordinating thousands of GPUs.
contributions: GPU-Direct Collective (GDC) framework for scaling collective operations
Demonstration of near-linear scaling performance on thousands of GPUs
Optimization of collective operations using GPU-direct and hardware offload
